summary: The Coordination of Rare Diseases at Sanford (CoRDS) is an international patient registry that serves as a centralized resource for rare disease research. Individuals affected by rare diseases, undiagnosed conditions, and disorders of unknown prevalence may voluntarily contribute health information to support natural history studies, participant recruitment, and other research efforts. Through partnerships with patient advocacy organizations and researchers worldwide, CoRDS helps connect rare disease communities with research opportunities while advancing knowledge across more than 7,000 rare diseases. Participation is free of charge.
desc:
The Coordination of Rare Diseases at Sanford (CoRDS) is an international, longitudinal patient registry for individuals affected by rare diseases, undiagnosed conditions, and disorders of unknown prevalence. Based at Sanford Research in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, CoRDS serves as a centralized resource that collects participant-reported demographic, contact, family history, and health information to support rare disease research.

Individuals with rare diseases, family members, caregivers, and carriers may enroll in the registry. Information collected through CoRDS supports research activities including natural history studies, epidemiologic investigations, characterization of disease burden, feasibility assessments, participant recruitment, and other efforts to advance understanding of rare diseases.

Registry data may be made available to qualified researchers following appropriate institutional review processes. CoRDS provides researchers access to a broad and geographically diverse population of individuals affected by rare diseases, helping facilitate study planning, participant identification, recruitment, and research collaboration. Access to CoRDS data is provided at no cost to qualified researchers.

CoRDS collaborates with rare disease patient advocacy organizations to increase awareness of the registry, support patient engagement, and help connect researchers with rare disease communities. CoRDS may also share select participant information with participating advocacy organizations when authorized by the participant and in accordance with applicable registry policies and agreements.

Participants may choose to be contacted regarding research opportunities that may be relevant to their condition. CoRDS serves as a resource for patients, families, researchers, healthcare professionals, patient advocacy organizations, and other stakeholders working to advance research across thousands of rare diseases.

Participation in CoRDS is voluntary and free of charge. Participants may withdraw from the registry at any time. CoRDS conducts periodic follow-up with participants to maintain current information, confirm continued participation, and support ongoing research efforts. For participants enrolled by a parent or legally authorized representative, CoRDS will seek consent directly from the participant upon reaching the age of majority, as applicable.

Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of a rare disease, a disease of unknown prevalence, undiagnosed or an unaffected carrier of a rare/uncommon disease

Exclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of a disease which is not rare

primary.m: To accelerate research into rare disorders by connecting individuals who are interested in research and who have been diagnosed with a rare disorder (or a disorder of unknown prevalence, or who are undiagnosed) with researchers who study rare diseases.

x.titre: CoRDS : registre international de patients atteints de maladies rares (Sanford)
x.question: Comment connecter les personnes atteintes de maladies rares aux chercheurs pour accélérer la recherche ?
x.contexte:
Les maladies rares, plus de 7 000 selon le registre, sont individuellement peu fréquentes, ce qui rend difficiles le recrutement des patients, la connaissance de l'histoire naturelle et la réalisation d'essais. Les données sont dispersées entre de nombreux centres.

Le registre CoRDS (Coordination of Rare Diseases at Sanford), basé à Sanford Research (Sioux Falls, Dakota du Sud), recueille de façon volontaire et gratuite des informations déclarées par les participants : données démographiques, antécédents familiaux et état de santé. Les personnes atteintes d'une maladie rare, non diagnostiquée ou de prévalence inconnue, leurs proches, leurs aidants et les porteurs peuvent s'y inscrire.

Le registre s'appuie sur des associations de patients et des chercheurs du monde entier. Les données, accessibles gratuitement à des chercheurs qualifiés après revue institutionnelle, servent aux études d'histoire naturelle, à l'épidémiologie, aux études de faisabilité et au recrutement. Il est cité dans cette liste à cause des maladies rares systémiques qu'il couvre (par ex. maladie de Kawasaki, myasthénie, maladie d'Addison).
x.interet: Le registre facilite la recherche sur les maladies rares et l'identification de participants pour des études. Il ne teste aucun traitement et n'a pas d'impact direct sur la pratique.
x.profil: Des personnes, de tout âge, atteintes d'une maladie rare, non diagnostiquée ou de prévalence inconnue, ainsi que des porteurs.

x.critere: Accélération de la recherche sur les maladies rares en reliant les personnes intéressées aux chercheurs.
